sources.observed_fact: WAL allows readers and a writer to proceed concurrently, but SQLite still permits only one writer at a time. WAL requires processes to share a host and does not work on a network filesystem; checkpointing affects WAL size and performance.
sources.limitation: Documentation describes SQLite behavior, not measured performance on the target ORA6.

sources.observed_fact: SQLite documents FTS5 as its full-text search extension.
sources.limitation: This does not establish search quality or capacity for the expected corpus.

sources.observed_fact: PostgreSQL documents SKIP LOCKED as avoiding waits on locked rows, while warning it produces an inconsistent view unsuitable for general-purpose querying.
sources.limitation: It is a queue-claim building block, not a complete job scheduler.

sources.observed_fact: The PostgreSQL manual has a dedicated full-text search chapter.
sources.limitation: No comparative benchmark against SQLite was performed.

sources.observed_fact: The current Streamable HTTP spec describes one MCP endpoint accepting POST requests; responses can be JSON or request-scoped SSE. It requires validating Origin and recommends authentication; local servers should bind to localhost. The spec notes removal of the GET stream endpoint and protocol-level sessions in this revision.
sources.limitation: Client compatibility must be checked against the actual MCP clients selected for deployment.

sources.observed_fact: Cloudflare documents publishing a self-hosted app through Tunnel with Access policies, recommends creating the Access application before its tunnel route, and describes validating the Access token at the origin to reject bypass traffic.
sources.limitation: This is product guidance, not an assessment of the target account, DNS, or Access configuration.

sources.observed_fact: SSE is a one-way server-to-client stream; events are UTF-8 text blocks separated by blank lines, and EventSource reconnects unless closed.
sources.limitation: SSE alone does not provide durable event storage or client-to-server controls.

sources.observed_fact: n8n documents workflow executions and execution-data redaction that hides inputs and outputs while preserving metadata such as status, timing, and node names.
sources.limitation: This page does not establish how n8n implements canvas telemetry internally.

recommendations.decision: PROPOSAL: Start with a small Python API and worker processes on the single ARM64 host; use local SQLite for authoritative metadata, jobs, events, and FTS5. Enable WAL, keep all database users on that host and on a local filesystem, use short write transactions, and monitor/checkpoint WAL. Treat this as a fit hypothesis, not a benchmark result.
recommendations.basis: The stated 4 CPU, 24 GB RAM, 22 GB available storage, and single-host starting point favor fewer moving parts. SQLite’s documented one-writer constraint is acceptable only while measured write contention remains low.

recommendations.decision: PROPOSAL: Store original artifacts as content-addressed blobs (SHA-256) with create-only writes, atomic publication, size limits, and a manifest recording hash, timestamps, adapter, collection parameters, and custody events. Keep normalized derivatives separate and link them to source hashes. Use append-only observation, claim, hypothesis, and evidence-link tables; model typed graph edges relationally and index approved searchable text with FTS5.
recommendations.basis: This gives reproducible provenance and relational integrity without a graph service. Hash checks and append-only application behavior are tamper-evident controls, not protection against a privileged host administrator.

recommendations.decision: PROPOSAL: Persist versioned DAGs, tasks, dependencies, idempotency keys, attempt counts, lease owner/expiry, adapter budgets, and an ordered event log. Claim due tasks in a short BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; heartbeat leases and recover expired work. Re-run only safe/idempotent operations; classify uncertain external mutations as needs_reconciliation. Enforce per-run limits for requests, bytes, wall time, concurrency, and storage before dispatch.
recommendations.basis: Persisted claims survive process restarts. SQLite leases coordinate same-host processes, but do not create multi-host capacity.

recommendations.decision: PROPOSAL: Make each API adapter independently disabled by default, with explicit enablement, scoped credentials, request/time/response limits, and audit events. Provide authenticated MCP Streamable HTTP with role-scoped tools, Origin validation, localhost binding when local, and no path or arbitrary-shell tools. Keep user-interface SSE telemetry separate from MCP transport.

PROPOSAL: Persist workflow versions and execution events. Emit status/progress pulses only when workers actually record transitions or heartbeats; serve an initial snapshot and replayable SSE cursor, plus keepalives. Provide authenticated POST controls for pause/cancel. Render source content as untrusted text and expose execution redaction controls.

PROPOSAL: Put the UI behind Cloudflare Access and Tunnel; validate Access identity at the origin too. Use separate least-privilege analyst, operator, and administrator roles; require explicit authorization for adapter configuration and destructive actions. For fetch adapters, allow only approved public HTTP(S) targets, reject loopback/private/link-local/reserved IPs, validate every redirect and DNS resolution, cap response bytes/time, and restrict egress. Keep secrets out of logs, events, prompts, and browser storage.
recommendations.basis: Cloudflare specifically warns that a tunnel route without an Access application can expose the app and recommends origin token validation.

recommendations.decision: PROPOSAL: Keep database and blob storage on the local persistent volume; set per-project quotas and stop acquisition before disk exhaustion. With 22 GB currently available, reserve explicit OS/database/recovery headroom and alert before crossing that threshold. Deploy a versioned ARM64 service build with additive, backward-compatible schema migrations. Back up using SQLite’s supported backup mechanism or a quiesced consistent copy plus blobs; verify restore before upgrades and retain the prior application build for rollback.

alternatives.use_when: Move authoritative jobs and metadata when measured write contention, multi-host workers, or operational needs justify a database service. Claim work with short row-lock transactions and SKIP LOCKED, restricted to queue selection; keep idempotency and lease recovery in application logic. PostgreSQL also offers full-text search.
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds an independently operated service and backup/upgrade path; not justified solely by the current host specification.

alternatives.use_when: Potential later broker/cache for measured fan-out or ephemeral coordination.
alternatives.tradeoff: Do not make it the initial source of truth: evidence provenance, typed relationships, search, and durable task state would still need a canonical store. Redis persistence-specific guarantees were not researched in this bounded pass.

alternatives.use_when: Only when a second host or availability requirement exists; move canonical state to PostgreSQL and use an appropriately durable object store, with explicit event delivery and idempotent consumers.
alternatives.tradeoff: More failure modes and operational burden than the one-host requirement establishes.

rejected: PROPOSAL: Starting with a graph database, Redis-only scheduler, or multiple distributed services before measured workload requires them.
PROPOSAL: Calling the artifact store immutable against privileged host access; local hashing and append-only controls do not provide that guarantee.
PROPOSAL: Showing synthetic progress pulses or treating a lease timeout as proof that an external action did not happen.
unknowns: Actual adapter count, expected request rates, artifact size distribution, retention period, and required concurrent analysts.
Measured CPU, memory, storage throughput, and SQLite write contention on the specific ARM64 OS and disk.
Access identity provider, DNS ownership, MCP client compatibility, and the desired external user model.
Provider terms, rate limits, and permitted data retention for each future adapter.
Whether regulatory or evidentiary requirements demand independently administered object lock, signatures, or external timestamping.
Redis persistence behavior was not verified from primary documentation in this bounded research pass.
tests: On the target ARM64 host, run a representative ingestion/search/DAG workload; record latency, CPU/RAM, WAL growth, checkpoint behavior, free space, and writer-busy rates before raising concurrency.
Crash during blob staging and metadata commit; verify no partial artifact is published, hashes match, duplicate content is safely deduplicated, and quota exhaustion stops collection.

Run competing claimers in separate local processes; assert a task is leased once, dependencies gate execution, idempotency conflicts reject, heartbeat/expiry recovers safe work, and ambiguous mutations require reconciliation.
Verify typed graph traversal, claim-to-source provenance, FTS search, and that normalized derivatives never replace raw artifacts.
Disable one adapter and confirm zero outbound calls; test SSRF cases including private IPs, DNS rebinding, redirects, oversized bodies, timeouts, and secret redaction.
Test MCP unauthenticated/under-scoped requests, invalid Origin rejection, tool authorization, and current Streamable HTTP JSON/SSE behavior with selected clients.
Assert UI SSE pulses correspond to persisted worker events, replay from cursor after reconnect, and controls require authorization; test redacted execution views.
Test Access denial at the edge and origin-side token validation, backup/restore of database plus blobs, migration rollback, and service rollback.
